caption:
🚂 Western Europe's railways, every line at its real opening date — 1825 → today.

Britain lays the first lines, then the continent catches up fast: by 1937 the countries on this map run about 217,000 km of track 🗺️ After that the tide turns. Cars and lorries win the short routes and thousands of branch lines close: the UK falls from about 26,000 km to 15,000, France from about 37,000 to 29,000. The faded lines are the ones that closed; today about 182,000 km remain in service.

📊 Data: OpenHistoricalMap (opening and closure dates) + OpenStreetMap (gaps), ODbL; Spain: Esteban-Oliver & Martí-Henneberg (DATA917). Coverage is uneven by country, and some lines in the Balkans and Luxembourg carry an estimated opening year (Wikidata). Switzerland is left blank: fewer than half of its lines are dated in the source.
🌍 Land: Natural Earth
